public_rationale: Pro subscription losses do not establish that every OpenAI user lost money. Reporting of positive paid-user compute margins also cannot settle the claim: it concerns different dates and a narrower cost measure. The searched records do not establish either universal user losses or a profitable user under a consistent definition during the target quarter.
limitations: News reporting substitutes for unavailable underlying financial records.
The cost allocation and observation period are evaluator interpretations.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI loses money on every single user.

statement.excerpt: As a reminder: OpenAI loses money on every single user.
statement.document_title: OpenAI Is A Systemic Risk To The Tech Industry

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that revenue attributable to each individual user falls short of the costs attributable to serving that user. A company-wide loss divided by user count does not establish this.
Use January through March 2025, the latest completed calendar quarter before publication, for the unspecified ongoing period.
Treat the financial basis as an estimate because the surrounding argument relies on reported financial estimates.
The statement does not specify how research, training and other shared expenses should be allocated to individual users.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable user-level records establish negative attributable profit for every user in the target period. Negative averages for the company or one subscription tier are insufficient.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records identify at least one profitable user, or a profitable user cohort whose consistently measured aggregate profit necessarily implies at least one profitable member, during the target period.

evidence.explanation: The article reports that Altman described Pro subscriptions as unprofitable. A loss for that tier does not establish a loss on every subscriber or other OpenAI user.

evidence.locator: Paragraph following the paid-user compute-margin comparison
evidence.explanation: The report describes positive paid-user compute margins at the end of 2024 and in October 2025. This cautions against treating company losses as universal user losses, but neither observation measures the target quarter or fully allocated user profit.
